summary: The Phase-21 metered round RAN and is fully recorded. 36 runs, 4 cells, 3 suites, $29.04, claude-opus-4-8 at effort high, user-approved after the zero-spend canary passed with ZERO SKIPs. HEADLINE: no correctness lift and no test-design lift from PASSIVE skill content -- pooled Pass@1 0.67 for all three arms after every defensible correction, and blind-judge substance 9/9 for the baseline on the three judgeable cells. The baseline is at ceiling. Non-null findings are all off the output axis: auto-trigger fired in 9 of 12 opportunities (an ABSOLUTE rate; comparing it to no_skill 0/12 is a non-comparison because firing is impossible without --plugin-dir), treated arms cost +23% output tokens and more turns, and the round's only 2 production edits both came from skill-bearing arms, which points AGAINST coach-don't-drive. A follow-up Opus 5 probe (3 runs, $2.44, user-approved) confirmed auto-trigger still fires 3/3 on the current model. THEN a quick task (260728-1pj) asked to run the forcing-function probe and instead found a BLOCKING self-contradiction in the shipped lz-red skill; the fix was drafted twice, reviewed twice, and REVERTED both times. plugins/lz-tdd is byte-unchanged. The 7-item fix spec is preserved and ready to implement.

decisions.decision: Report RXF as TWO numbers -- 9/9 behaviourally red, 0/9 under the differential -- and change nothing in the gate.
decisions.rationale: All 9 runs collected and failed on an attributed assertion; the runner masks type diagnostics and the repo has no typecheck target, so the gate failed them on a standard the target never applies. A precedence rule to fix it was TESTED against the negative control and REJECTED: canary-compile also records attributed_failures 1, so the rule would flip a control to pass. The only mechanical separator is a baseline-keyed rule, already ruled out. The fix is reporting, not the gate.

decisions.decision: RXL stays excluded from the correctness headline; its committed numbers stand.
decisions.rationale: Its only 2 passes are its only 2 production edits -- both created RDX_LOCALE and then asserted it. Blind judge 0/9 on both substance dims; no specimen rendered anything. Confirmed independently three ways.

decisions.decision: The gate is stricter than every owned source, and that is recorded as deliberate EVAL DESIGN, never as doctrinal fidelity.
decisions.rationale: No owned source requires the red to be an assertion failure. The gate does, because the eval exists to measure whether the model pinned the missing BEHAVIOUR. Honest labelling preserves both the numbers and the doctrine.

decisions.decision: Revert both draft red-bar fixes rather than ship a third attempt in a deep session.
decisions.rationale: Four consecutive proposals were killed by gates, none by inspection. The second review showed the diagnosis itself (the execution axis) was wrong for Vitest + TS, so a third attempt is a fresh start on a different line, not a finish. The defect has existed since Phase 18; one more day is not the risk. Shipping a wrong doctrine fix to a public skill is.

context_notes: MEASURE, DO NOT REASON fired repeatedly and expensively this session. Five of my own conclusions were overturned by measurement or by a gate, none by my own inspection: (1) I called the SRVC failures a model problem before reading added_test_titles -- they were an instrument false negative on the target's own test.skipIf idiom; (2) I called RXF structurally invalid before checking canary-rdxf-red, which proves a compiling route exists; (3) I said the models followed the house idiom on RXF -- jest-dom is a 1-of-142 outlier and the dominant compiling form sits in 90 of 142 files; (4) I flattened the lz-refactor history into 'five null probes' and omitted the sixth, which FLIPPED the axis and shipped; (5) four successive red-bar fixes died to gates. The pattern is always the same: inferring from adjacent evidence instead of running the direct check. ALSO: my throwaway analysis scripts were error-prone all session -- a require path, an ESM URL scheme, a double-escaped regex, two guessed field names, and twice a diff-extraction bug. Every one was caught by cross-checking against an independent signal, never by inspection, and the plus-lines-only extraction bug was caught ONLY because a judge verdict contradicted the mechanical gate. Treat a judge disagreeing with the gate as a signal to audit the harness, not the model. The unbiased reviewers were worth more than everything else combined: one recomputed all 36 runs and matched mechanical-red.json to the digit while overturning four of my conclusions, and one killed a doctrine edit by importing classify() and grading two stub shapes in about 30 seconds.
